lead.title: Three generations at one stove, now cooking in Dallas
paragraphs: Chaska serves desi food with a Punjabi tadka, cooked from family recipes that were never written down. They were watched, tasted and corrected across three generations, and they arrive at your table unchanged: dal simmered overnight, saag stirred through the afternoon, rotis off the tawa when you sit down.
Everything is served family style, in the middle of the table, meant to be passed and shared.

figure.caption: Naan on the wall of the clay tandoor, baked to order through service.

dishes.name: Dal Makhani
dishes.description: Black lentils put on the flame the night before, finished with butter. The recipe is Ronika’s grandmother’s, and it is not negotiable.

dishes.name: Tandoori Murgh
dishes.description: Chicken marinated in yogurt and Kashmiri chili, roasted in the clay tandoor that is lit every morning.

dishes.name: Sarson da Saag
dishes.description: Mustard greens cooked slowly with ginger and garlic, served with makki di roti and white butter, the way winter demands.

family.title: Recipes taught by hand, kept by memory
paragraphs: Owner Ronika Singh learned every dish on this menu in her family’s kitchen, measured in handfuls and pinches. The chhole are her mother’s. The butter chicken is the house recipe her family has argued over and perfected for decades. Her rule is simple: cook it the way it was taught, or leave it off the menu.
The family is all here, including Snoopy, the house shih tzu and honorary sous chef, who supervises the dining room and greets regulars by the door.

figure.caption: The table, mid dinner. Dishes land in the middle and get passed.

cateringNotice.title: The same food, for your gathering
cateringNotice.body: From family dinners to weddings, we cater the menu we serve in the restaurant, prepared for your guests and delivered ready to serve.
